i0: ***Will*** + base verb is one of the main ways to talk about the future in English: *I**'ll** call you tomorrow. It **will** be sunny at the weekend.*
i1: But *will* isn't the only future form, and it isn't always the right one. For plans, see [Be Going To](/blog/grammar/be-going-to/), and for choosing, see [Will vs Going To](/blog/grammar/will-vs-going-to/).
wsh-form.t: Will and won't: form and future facts
wsh-form.s: **will / won't + base verb**, the same for every person: *I'll be 30 next year. She won't be here tomorrow.*
wsh-form.b1: *Will* is the same for all persons and is followed by the **base verb**, with no *to*: *She **will come**.* Not *She wills come* or *will to come*.
wsh-form.b2: We use it for **facts** about the future and things we're sure about: *Tomorrow **will** be Monday. The sun **will** set at 6.45.*
wsh-decisions-offers.t: Instant decisions, offers, promises and requests
wsh-decisions-offers.s: Use **will** when you decide at the moment of speaking (*I'll have the soup*), and for offers (*I'll help*), promises (*I'll call you*) and requests (*Will you…?*).
wsh-decisions-offers.b0.1.1: *Your bags look heavy. I**'ll** carry one.*
wsh-decisions-offers.b1: When we decide something **at the moment of speaking**, we use *will*, not the present simple: *The phone's ringing. ~ I**'ll** get it.* Not *I get it*.
wsh-decisions-offers.b2: If the decision was made **before**, use *be going to*: *I**'m going to** paint the kitchen this weekend.* (I decided last week.) See [Will vs Going To](/blog/grammar/will-vs-going-to/).
wsh-predictions.t: Predictions: I think it will…, probably
wsh-predictions.s: Use **will** for predictions based on opinion or experience, often with *I think, I'm sure, probably, I expect*: *I think it'll be a great party.*
wsh-predictions.b0: We often use *will* to say what we **think** or **believe** about the future: *I think Brazil **will** win the World Cup. You**'ll** love this film.*
wsh-predictions.b1: Common phrases: *I think / I don't think, I'm sure, I expect, I hope, probably, definitely, perhaps*.
wsh-predictions.b2: Word order: ***probably / definitely*** go **after** *will* but **before** *won't*: *She**'ll probably** be late. She **probably won't** come.*
wsh-predictions.b3: For a negative prediction, say ***I don't think … will***, not *I think … won't*: *I **don't think** it **will** rain.* (more natural than *I think it won't rain*)
wsh-shall.t: Shall: offers, suggestions and formal rules
wsh-shall.s: **Shall I / shall we** + base verb for offers and suggestions (mainly British). In formal documents, **shall** = must: *The tenant shall pay the rent monthly.*
wsh-shall.b0: ***Shall I…?*** offers help, and ***Shall we…?*** makes a suggestion: ***Shall I** carry your bag? **Shall we** go for a walk?* It's also used to ask for advice: *What **shall** I do?*
wsh-shall.b1: *Shall* with *I / we* for the future (*I shall be there*) is formal and old-fashioned in British English. Most people say *I'll* or *I will*.
wsh-shall.b2: In **legal and formal documents**, ***shall*** expresses an obligation: *The company **shall** provide training to all staff.*
wsh-shall.b3: In American English, *shall* is rare in conversation. Americans usually say ***Should I…?*** or ***Do you want me to…?*** for offers, and ***Should we…?*** or ***Let's…*** for suggestions.
wsh-shall.w1: shall is used with I / we
